tagline: Private days on Japan’s quiet island.

home.heroTitle: Walk Shikoku with someone who lives here.
home.heroLead: Small private tours through Iya Valley, pilgrimage trails, and the Seto Inland Sea — at a human pace, in English or Dutch.
home.introTitle: The island most visitors skip. That’s the point.
home.introBody: Shikoku is still a place of farm roads, cedar forests, and temple bells. I take a handful of guests each week into the valleys and coastline I know well — no bus groups, no ticking checklist. We eat where locals eat, walk where the buses don’t go, and leave room for weather and curiosity.
home.availabilityBody: Green days are open for a private tour. Red days are already booked. Grey days are off — unlisted dates stay unavailable until I mark them open.
home.aboutTitle: A Dutch guide on a Japanese island
home.aboutBody: I moved to Tokushima more than a decade ago. Shikoku is not a backdrop I learned from a guidebook; it’s where I buy vegetables, hike on my days off, and take my own visitors. If you want a polished megaphone tour, I’m not your person. If you want a thoughtful day with someone who can talk to the farmer and the priest, write to me.
home.finalTitle: Tell me the days you have.
home.finalBody: There is no checkout. Send a few sentences — who you are, what you hope to see, when you’re here — and I’ll reply by email.

footer.blurb: Private walking and driving tours across Shikoku. English and Dutch. No live booking — inquiries by email.

toursPage.title: Choose a day, not a package.
toursPage.lead: Each outing is for your group only. Prices are per group, not per person, unless noted. I adapt the route to fitness, weather, and what you actually want to see.

aboutPage.title: Sven — Shikoku, at walking speed.
aboutPage.lead: I grew up in the Netherlands, live in Tokushima Prefecture, and spend most of my working days on mountain roads, temple paths, and the edges of the Inland Sea.
body: Guests often ask how a Dutch person ended up guiding in Shikoku. The short version: I came for a season, stayed for the island, and slowly became the person friends asked to “just show us around.” That informal habit became this work.

I speak English and Dutch with guests, and Japanese with everyone we meet. That matters more than it sounds. A vineyard owner, a temple caretaker, a woman selling udon at a roadside stall — the day is better when we can actually talk.

I take private groups only. Four people is a sweet spot; six is the usual maximum. I drive, I walk, I pack a thermos. I do not run a call centre or a booking engine. If I’m already out with someone, that date is red on the calendar.

When I’m not guiding I am usually in the hills, at the market, or on a stool somewhere with a bowl of noodles. Shikoku rewards people who stay a little longer than the itinerary suggests. I try to build days that feel like that.

availabilityPage.title: Open days, plainly marked.
availabilityPage.lead: Green is available. Red is booked. Grey is unavailable. Dates I have not listed stay off. This is not a reservation system — if a day looks free, still send an inquiry so we can confirm.
availabilityPage.note: I update this calendar by editing a JSON file in the site. If something looks stale, email me; I’ll correct it.

contactPage.title: Write as if to a person. You are.
contactPage.lead: I read every message myself. Tell me roughly when you are on Shikoku, how many of you there are, and what kind of day you want. I’ll answer by email — usually within a day or two.

legalPage.title: Privacy and terms
privacy: This site does not use a database or user accounts. The contact form sends your name, email, dates, group size, tour of interest, and message to me by email (via Resend). I use that information only to answer your inquiry and arrange a tour.
I do not sell your data. I do not run advertising pixels. Analytics, if enabled, is privacy-oriented traffic measurement from Vercel.
If you want a message deleted from my inbox after we’ve finished corresponding, email me and I will do so.
terms: Inquiries are not bookings. A date is confirmed only when I write back and we agree in email.
Prices on tour pages are indicative and in Japanese yen unless stated otherwise. Final price depends on group size, season, and route.
Tours may be adjusted or postponed for typhoons, landslides, or other safety reasons. I’ll discuss options with you if that happens.
You are responsible for your own travel insurance and for being fit enough for the day we plan.
